assertions_contracts.best_practice: The hand-rolled sentinel pattern the guide prescribes now has a standard form: PEP 661's built-in sentinel type shipped in Python 3.15, designed exactly to distinguish 'argument omitted' from an explicit None with a readable repr.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Still unapplied from run 1 (the addendum records these proposals as adoption decisions for Matt, not remediation). assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert only for programmer invariants (python -O strips assert, so external rejection must be an explicit raise that survives -O); use a unique hand-rolled sentinel object to distinguish an omitted argument from explicit None; no mutation/authorization inside assert (guide sections 4 and 8).

bounded_work.best_practice: No official Python source prescribes budgets; nothing contradicts it. 3.15's lazy imports and UTF-8-by-default change startup/encoding behaviour, not bounding obligations.
bounded_work.evidence: Tiger policy stricter than mainstream by design; no contradicting official position in the 3.14 What's New document or the 3.15 announcement, both fetched live this pass.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named UPPER_SNAKE_CASE bounds for input bytes, item counts, nesting depth, retries, queues and captured output; no unbounded list(iterator) or task creation; retries need idempotency, a shared deadline, bounded backoff and injected jitter (guide section 5).

concurrency.best_practice: PEP 779 made free-threaded Python officially supported in 3.14, 3.15 adds a stable ABI for free-threaded extensions (PEP 803/820/793), and PEP 734 (3.14) put multiple interpreters (concurrent.interpreters, InterpreterPoolExecutor) in the stdlib as an isolation mechanism between threads and processes.
concurrency.evidence: Run-1 stale verdict REMEDIATED and verified in current text (pass-2 item 11): section 2 and section 21 now carry exactly the facts above. What's New in 3.14 fetched live this pass confirms the PEP 734 and PEP 779 listings, and the 3.15 announcement confirms the free-threaded stable ABI.
concurrency.guide_position: asyncio.TaskGroup for related tasks with admission bounded before creation; re-check state after every await; cleanup in finally and re-raise CancelledError; processes for killable untrusted work; never assume the GIL. Section 2 now describes free-threaded CPython as officially supported in 3.14 (PEP 779) with a stable ABI for free-threaded extensions in 3.15, and section 21 now covers PEP 734 multiple interpreters beside the TaskGroup/process guidance.

error_handling.best_practice: Matches current documented practice; 3.14/3.15 error-message improvements do not change exception semantics or chaining guidance.
error_handling.evidence: No exception-model change in What's New 3.14 or the 3.15 announcement, both fetched live this pass.
error_handling.guide_position: Domain exception classes (or one explicit result type) per boundary; catch only what the layer can interpret; chain with raise DomainError(...) from exc; never swallow BaseException — interrupts and cancellation propagate; state whether failure leaves state unchanged or partial (guide section 7).

memory_ownership.best_practice: PEP 814 (Python 3.15) adds a built-in frozendict: a genuinely immutable, hashable mapping, which is a stronger primitive than the guide's frozen-dataclass-with-caveats approach for config/records that must not mutate.
memory_ownership.evidence: Still unapplied from run 1. Verified by full read this pass: section 10 retains only the frozen-dataclass caveat and the guide contains no frozendict mention. The official 3.15 announcement fetched live lists PEP 814 among the major new features.
memory_ownership.guide_position: Context managers (ExitStack/AsyncExitStack) own resources; never rely on __del__; bound caches/logs/queues; frozen dataclass preferred for records, with the explicit caveat that it is not recursively immutable when a field holds a list (guide sections 10, 14 and 15).

security.best_practice: The prohibitions hold, but 3.14 added a mechanism the guide's security section lacks: PEP 750 template strings (t-strings) return a Template separating static text from interpolations specifically so processors can sanitize/parameterize (SQL, HTML, logging) instead of concatenating untrusted values into a finished string.
security.evidence: Still unapplied from run 1. Verified by full read this pass: section 18 contains no t-string or Template guidance. What's New in 3.14 fetched live this pass describes t-strings producing string.templatelib.Template objects whose parts stay separate before combination, and explicitly notes the sanitising use for user input and safe SQL construction.
security.guide_position: Never pickle.loads untrusted bytes or eval/exec external text; parameterized SQL; argv arrays with shell=False; validated URL schemes; venv is not a sandbox; subprocess with explicit argv/cwd/env/deadline/output bounds and a cleanup owner (guide sections 18 and 20).

static_analysis.best_practice: mypy --strict remains a valid gate, but the field moved: Astral's ty (Rust, type checker + language server, from the Ruff/uv team) is in beta with Astral using it exclusively in its own projects and recommending it to motivated production users, and Meta's Pyrefly is stable at 1.x — the guide's 'choose one authoritative checker (mypy, or Pyright/basedpyright)' menu predates both.
static_analysis.evidence: Still unapplied from run 1. Verified by full-text search this pass: the guide's only checker-policy sentence (section 27) still names mypy and Pyright/basedpyright only. Astral's ty announcement fetched live confirms the beta status and Astral's exclusive in-house use; the facebook/pyrefly repo confirms Pyrefly's development status is stable (1.0.0, May 2026).
static_analysis.guide_position: Gate on mypy --strict; if Pyright/basedpyright is also used, choose one authoritative policy and explain differences instead of suppressing globally; Ruff provides lint diagnostics only (no type checking) in the guide's pairing (guide section 27).

testing.guide_position: unittest or a reviewed runner; boundary cases (missing/false/zero/empty/max/oversize/wrong type/negative/exhaustion); validation also run under python -O; async timeout/cancellation/sibling-failure/stale-generation tests; property tests with bounded generators and reproducible seeds (guide section 28).

proposals.evidence: Carried from run 1, still unapplied (full-text search this pass: no sentinel-type or frozendict mention in the guide). proposals.proposal: On a 3.15 baseline, replace the hand-rolled 'unique sentinel object' idiom with the built-in sentinel type (PEP 661) for omitted-vs-None parameters, and offer frozendict (PEP 814) as the immutable-mapping primitive alongside frozen dataclasses where a mapping must be genuinely immutable and hashable.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt when the floor rises to 3.15; keep the hand-rolled idiom documented for 3.12-3.14 targets.

proposals.evidence: Carried from run 1, still unapplied (section 18 unchanged). proposals.proposal: Add t-strings (PEP 750, Python 3.14+) to the security section: for SQL, HTML and structured logging construction, accept a Template and process its interpolations (parameterize/escape) rather than receiving a pre-concatenated f-string, which destroys the static/interpolated distinction the check depends on.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as the preferred pattern for new 3.14+ code at injection boundaries; f-string-built queries stay banned as they already effectively are.
